7.1.cite: Lastella, M., O'Mullan, C., Paterson, J. L., & Reynolds, A. C. (2019). Sex and sleep: Perceptions of sex as a sleep promoting behavior in the general adult population. Frontiers in Public Health, 7, Article 33.
7.1.uses: In an online survey of 778 adults, the authors ran chi square analyses to see whether men and women differed in their reported sleep quality and sleep onset after different sexual activities.

7.2.cite: Malykh, S., Demareva, V., Malykh, A., Ismatullina, V. I., Adamovich, T., Kolyasnikov, P., et al. (2026). Post-COVID-19 consequences and psychological well-being in students: The mediating role of trait anxiety. Behavioral Sciences, 16(6), 996.
7.2.uses: The authors split 7,482 students into three groups (no COVID-19, COVID-19 without lasting consequences, COVID-19 with lasting consequences) and compared them with ANOVA followed by Tukey post hoc tests.

7.3.cite: Alromaih, Y., Aldakhil, S., Alsaloom, D., Alkhalaf, G. A., & Alshehi, R. (2026). Effectiveness of health exhibitions on knowledge and attitudes toward nutrition and disease prevention in Saudi Arabia: An intervention study. Frontiers in Public Health, 14, Article 1827711.
7.3.uses: The Shapiro-Wilk test showed the knowledge and attitude scores were not normal and partly ordinal, so the authors used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for before and after scores and Mann-Whitney U and Kruskal-Wallis tests for group comparisons.

8.1.cite: Hirano, Y. O., Tamagawa, R., & Matsumoto, T. (2022). Factors influencing the psychological independence of retired community-dwelling older adults in Japan. Frontiers in Psychology, 13, Article 1004645.
8.1.uses: In a questionnaire study of 246 older adults, the authors used Pearson's correlation coefficient, alongside t-tests and multiple regression, to examine how psychological independence relates to other measured variables.

8.2.cite: Eriksson, K., Strimling, P., & Vartanova, I. (2023). Appropriateness ratings of everyday behaviors in the United States now and 50 years ago. Frontiers in Psychology, 14, Article 1237494.
8.2.uses: The authors ran a simple linear regression of the overall appropriateness rating of 37 everyday behaviors on a single externalities and internalities index, and reported the slope B with its confidence interval. This is a close match for slope only; I did not confirm that an intercept is reported.

8.3.cite: Liang, N., Wang, X., Ren, J., Zhang, Y., Liu, X., Ka, L., et al. (2026). Examining the status quo and related factors of clinical nurses' spare-time planning. Frontiers in Public Health, 14, Article 1798726.
8.3.uses: For their linear regression of nurses' spare-time planning, the authors reported R squared and adjusted R squared, then checked residuals with a normal P-P plot and a plot of standardized residuals against predicted values to judge normality and constant variance.

8.4.cite: Zoghlami, W., Hawani, A., Khiari, H., Mnedla, S., Marsigliante, S., Elloumi, A., et al. (2023). The relationship between emotional intelligence, anxiety, and performance in physical education and sport students. Frontiers in Psychology, 14, Article 1236070.
8.4.uses: With 350 students, the authors first ran simple linear regressions and then a multiple regression with several anxiety and emotional intelligence subscales entered together to study what relates to exam performance.

8.5.cite: Gaskell, C., Sarada, P., Aleem, E., & Bendriss, G. (2023). Identifying lifestyle factors associated to co-morbidity of obesity and psychiatric disorders, a pilot study. Frontiers in Public Health, 11, Article 1132994.
8.5.uses: The authors used multivariate logistic regression to see whether lifestyle habits such as alcohol, smoking, exercise and sleep predicted having both obesity and a mental health condition, and reported odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

9.1.cite: Ostacoli, L., Carletto, S., Cavallo, M., Baldomir-Gago, P., Di Lorenzo, G., Fernandez, I., et al. (2018). Comparison of eye movement desensitization reprocessing and cognitive behavioral therapy as adjunctive treatments for recurrent depression: The European Depression EMDR Network (EDEN) randomized controlled trial. Frontiers in Psychology, 9, Article 74.
9.1.uses: A single-blind randomized controlled trial in which 82 patients were randomized 1:1 to EMDR or CBT using a block-wise sequence generated by a central computer system, with allocation handled by a study coordinator.

9.2.cite: Alromaih, Y., Aldakhil, S., Alsaloom, D., Alkhalaf, G. A., & Alshehi, R. (2026). Effectiveness of health exhibitions on knowledge and attitudes toward nutrition and disease prevention in Saudi Arabia: An intervention study. Frontiers in Public Health, 14, Article 1827711.
9.2.uses: Before choosing tests, the authors checked the normality of the knowledge and attitude scores with the Shapiro-Wilk test and checked equal variances with Levene's test. Normality failed, so they switched to non-parametric tests.

9.3.cite: Santiago, P. H. R., Quintero, A., Haag, D., Roberts, R., Smithers, L., & Jamieson, L. (2021). Drop-the-p: Bayesian CFA of the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support in Australia. Frontiers in Psychology, 12, Article 542257.
9.3.uses: The authors fitted a Bayesian confirmatory factor analysis to survey data from 3,899 adults, reported 95% credible intervals for model fit and reliability, and used the Bayes factor to compare competing factor structures.
